slides.text: Detective Vance stared at the crime scene photos pinned to the board. Five victims across the city. No forced entry, no struggle, and every single mirror in their homes had been shattered into dust. The press called him The Glass Killer. I was the lead profiler on the case, exhausted and hitting a dead end. Vance handed me the final coroner's report. 'Look at the cause of death,' he said, his voice trembling. 'It's physically impossible.'

I scanned the file. Cause of death: internal lacerations. Thousands of microscopic glass shards found inside the victim's lungs and bloodstream. 'How did he force them to swallow it without leaving marks?' I asked. Vance shook his head. 'He didn't. There's no glass in their stomachs. It entered through their pores.' I rubbed my tired eyes, catching my reflection in the precinct window. The woman looking back at me blinked, even though I hadn't.

A cold dread paralyzed me. The reflection in the glass raised its hand, holding a jagged shard. I hadn't moved a muscle. 'Vance,' I whispered, backing away from the window. The reflection smiled, a horrific, bloody grin, and drove the shard into its own throat. Instantly, I felt a sharp, tearing agony erupt inside my windpipe. As I collapsed, choking on my own blood, I realized why the victims had tried to destroy all their mirrors.
